# Mary Vance

## Overview

- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v5 c6 P8](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0008)</sub>

## Appearance

She has crimped hair, a plump face, rosy cheeks, and shining white eyes. At times she has dressed up in a blue velvet cap with a scarlet rosette, a navy blue cloth coat, smart cloth-topped boots, and a squirrel-fur muff lined with red satin.

_Sources: [v5 c18 P5](../source/v05-c18.md#nw-v05-c18-p0005), [v5 c18 P7](../source/v05-c18.md#nw-v05-c18-p0007)_

## Personality

Mary Vance is loud, outspoken, and proud of her new clothes when she gets them. She has a strong, conventional streak of honesty, takes pride in working hard, and gets annoyed when good food is ruined. Despite being prone to telling gossip and asserting her opinions boldly, she can be a stimulating companion.

_Sources: [v5 c6 P14](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0014), [v5 c6 P18](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0018), [v5 c18 P5](../source/v05-c18.md#nw-v05-c18-p0005), [v5 c33 P1](../source/v05-c33.md#nw-v05-c33-p0001)_

## Traits

- Outspoken and opinionated  <sub>[v5 c33 P1](../source/v05-c33.md#nw-v05-c33-p0001), [v5 c33 P5](../source/v05-c33.md#nw-v05-c33-p0005)</sub>
- Proud of her clothes  <sub>[v5 c18 P5](../source/v05-c18.md#nw-v05-c18-p0005)</sub>
- Fear of ghosts  <sub>[v5 c6 P19](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0019)</sub>
- Dislike of cats  <sub>[v5 c6 P18](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0018)</sub>

## Abilities

- Basic literacy and math up to fractions  <sub>[v5 c6 P14](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0014)</sub>
- Cleans, mends, and sews neatly  <sub>[v5 c6 P5](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0005), [v5 c6 P15](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0015)</sub>
- Clear and strong singing voice  <sub>[v5 c6 P8](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0008)</sub>

## History

After running away, Mary Vance was found in an old barn by the Meredith children and brought to live at the manse. She accompanied the manse children to church wearing borrowed clothing, singing lustily in the pew and sticking her tongue out at Mrs. Milgrave when stared at. Refusing to attend school because she felt she had enough education, she stayed at the manse to clean, sweep, patch clothes, and attempt to put things in order. Though she tried to intervene in the household cooking, Aunt Martha kept control of the kitchen. She became a regular companion to the local children in Rainbow Valley, although she refused to play in the graveyard out of fear of ghosts and claimed to have seen hundreds of them. She frequently shared local town gossip, including rumors about Rosemary West, Norman Douglas, and community pranks.

_Sources: [v5 c6 P0](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0000), [v5 c6 P3](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0003), [v5 c6 P8](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0008), [v5 c6 P9](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0009), [v5 c6 P11](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0011), [v5 c6 P12](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0012), [v5 c6 P15](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0015), [v5 c6 P16](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0016), [v5 c6 P19](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0019), [v5 c6 P23](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0023), [v5 c18 P5](../source/v05-c18.md#nw-v05-c18-p0005), [v5 c33 P0](../source/v05-c33.md#nw-v05-c33-p0000), [v5 c33 P2](../source/v05-c33.md#nw-v05-c33-p0002), [v5 c33 P5](../source/v05-c33.md#nw-v05-c33-p0005), [v5 c33 P7](../source/v05-c33.md#nw-v05-c33-p0007), [v5 c33 P9](../source/v05-c33.md#nw-v05-c33-p0009)_

## Background by volume

- Lived over-harbour with Mrs. Wiley  <sub>[v5 c6 P1](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0001), [v5 c6 P10](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0010)</sub>
- Attended four winters of school while living with Mrs. Wiley  <sub>[v5 c6 P12](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0012)</sub>
- Was found as a ragged, runaway waif in the old Taylor barn by the Meredith children  <sub>[v5 c18 P5](../source/v05-c18.md#nw-v05-c18-p0005), [v5 c18 P7](../source/v05-c18.md#nw-v05-c18-p0007)</sub>

## Quotes

> Nope. I’ve finished my education. I went to school four winters since I come to Mrs. Wiley’s and I’ve had all I want of that. I’m sick and tired of being everlastingly jawed at ‘cause I didn’t get my home-lessons done. I’d no time to do home-lessons.  <sub>[v5 c6 P12](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0012)</sub>

> I can tell you if old Martha’d let me cook you’d have some decent meals. There’d be no more ‘ditto’—and no more lumpy porridge and blue milk either. What does she do with all the cream?  <sub>[v5 c6 P16](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0016)</sub>

> I’d like to cat her. I’ve no use for cats anyhow. They belong to the old Nick. You can tell that by their eyes. Well, if old Martha won’t, she won’t, I s’pose. But it gits on my nerves to see good vittles spoiled.  <sub>[v5 c6 P18](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0018)</sub>

> Do you know that Rosemary West won’t marry your pa because she thinks you are such a wild lot? She’s afraid she couldn’t bring you up right and so she turned him down.  <sub>[v5 c33 P2](../source/v05-c33.md#nw-v05-c33-p0002)</sub>
